guide.title: Route 66 from Chicago to Santa Monica
guide.author: friends of Placemoir
guide.summary: Nine days on the old Mother Road across eight states, with diners, neon motels, roadside giants and Route 66 museums from the Begin sign in Chicago to the end of the pier in Santa Monica.
sections: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Historic Route 66 Begin Sign
places.address: E Adams St & S Michigan Ave, Chicago, IL 60603
places.notes: The road starts on Adams Street across from the Art Institute, where a brown Begin sign marks mile zero. Westbound traffic leaves on Adams; the matching End sign is a block south on Jackson.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Lou Mitchell's
places.notes: A diner since 1923, a few blocks from the start of the road. Big omelets, double-yolk eggs and a free donut hole while you wait in line.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Dell Rhea's Chicken Basket
places.notes: A roadhouse serving fried chicken on this stretch of old 66 since the 1940s, now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Launching Pad Drive-In
places.notes: Home of the Gemini Giant, a fiberglass spaceman holding a rocket since the 1960s. The old drive-in building has been restored as a stop with food and Route 66 souvenirs.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Polk-a-Dot Drive In
places.notes: A 1950s burger stand with fiberglass statues of Elvis, Marilyn Monroe and the Blues Brothers out front. Order a malt and pose for the photo.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Illinois Route 66 Hall of Fame & Museum
places.notes: A free museum in Pontiac's old firehouse, with road artist Bob Waldmire's converted school bus and VW van parked out back. Look for the murals around the courthouse square.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Funks Grove Pure Maple Sirup
places.notes: A family that has tapped these maples since the 1800s and spells it sirup the old way. The shop keeps limited, seasonal hours, so check before you count on it.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Cozy Dog Drive In
places.notes: The family that claims the corn dog on a stick still runs this Springfield counter. The walls are covered with Route 66 memorabilia.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Lincoln Home National Historic Site
places.notes: The only house Abraham Lincoln ever owned, set in four restored blocks of his old neighborhood. Free ranger-led tours start at the visitor center.
places.section: Day 1 · Chicago to Springfield, Illinois · 200 mi

places.name: Ariston Cafe
places.notes: A dining room in a 1935 brick building that has served travelers on the road since the 1920s. Good for a sit-down lunch between Springfield and St. Louis.
places.section: Day 2 · Springfield, Illinois to Cuba, Missouri · 180 mi

places.name: Old Chain of Rocks Bridge
places.address: Chain of Rocks Rd, Granite City, IL 62040
places.notes: A mile-long former Route 66 bridge over the Mississippi, with a 22-degree bend in the middle, now open only to walkers and cyclists. Park on the Illinois side.
places.section: Day 2 · Springfield, Illinois to Cuba, Missouri · 180 mi

places.name: Gateway Arch National Park
places.notes: The 630-foot stainless steel arch on the riverfront, with a museum underneath and small tram pods to the top. Book tram times ahead on the official site.
places.section: Day 2 · Springfield, Illinois to Cuba, Missouri · 180 mi

places.name: Ted Drewes Frozen Custard
places.notes: A walk-up custard stand on Chippewa Street, an old 66 alignment, since 1941. Order a concrete, so thick it is handed over upside down. Closed for part of the winter.
places.section: Day 2 · Springfield, Illinois to Cuba, Missouri · 180 mi

places.name: Meramec Caverns
places.notes: The cave that painted its name on barn roofs all along the road. Guided tours walk through large lit chambers along the Meramec River.
places.section: Day 2 · Springfield, Illinois to Cuba, Missouri · 180 mi

places.name: Wagon Wheel Motel
places.notes: Stone cottages from the 1930s, restored with modern rooms and a working neon sign. Cuba's downtown murals are a short walk away.
places.section: Day 2 · Springfield, Illinois to Cuba, Missouri · 180 mi

places.name: Missouri Hick Bar-B-Que
places.notes: Barbecue smoked over hickory in a big log building next door to the Wagon Wheel. Easy dinner without moving the car.
places.section: Day 2 · Springfield, Illinois to Cuba, Missouri · 180 mi

places.name: Devil's Elbow Bridge
places.notes: A 1923 steel truss bridge over a tight bend of the Big Piney River on a bypassed loop of old 66. Pull off for the bluffs and the quiet.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: 66 Drive-In Theatre
places.notes: A 1949 drive-in movie screen still showing films on the old highway west of Carthage. It runs from spring to fall only; check the schedule.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: Cars on the Route
places.notes: A restored 1930s Kan-O-Tex service station on Kansas's short stretch of 66. The rusty tow truck out front helped inspire Mater in Cars.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: Rainbow Bridge
places.notes: The last surviving concrete Marsh arch bridge on Route 66, built in 1923 over Brush Creek. A newer road now runs alongside, so pull off and walk across for the photo.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: Coleman Theatre
places.notes: A 1929 Spanish Revival vaudeville house on Main Street with its original theater organ. Volunteers lead tours on most days; check the theater's site.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: Blue Whale of Catoosa
places.notes: A grinning 80-foot concrete whale built in the early 1970s as an anniversary gift, sitting in a spring-fed pond. A free photo stop.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: Cyrus Avery Route 66 Memorial Bridge and Centennial Plaza
places.notes: A plaza at the old 11th Street bridge honoring Tulsa's Cyrus Avery, who helped create Route 66, with a large bronze of a family car meeting a horse-drawn wagon.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: The Campbell Hotel
places.notes: A 1927 building on 11th Street, Tulsa's stretch of Route 66, restored as a boutique hotel with individually themed rooms.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: Tally's Good Food Cafe
places.notes: A neon-lit diner on 11th Street with chicken-fried steak, cinnamon rolls the size of a plate and breakfast all day.
places.section: Day 3 · Cuba, Missouri to Tulsa, Oklahoma · 290 mi

places.name: Rock Cafe
places.notes: A 1939 cafe built from sandstone dug up during road construction. Order a burger or the chicken-fried steak at the counter.
places.section: Day 4 · Tulsa to Elk City, Oklahoma · 210 mi

places.name: Arcadia Round Barn
places.notes: A big round red barn from 1898, restored by local volunteers, with a small museum downstairs and a dance loft upstairs.
places.section: Day 4 · Tulsa to Elk City, Oklahoma · 210 mi

places.name: POP's 66
places.notes: A modern gas station and diner under a 66-foot steel soda bottle that lights up at night. Inside, coolers hold hundreds of different sodas.
places.section: Day 4 · Tulsa to Elk City, Oklahoma · 210 mi

places.name: Lucille's Service Station
places.notes: A 1929 two-story gas station where Lucille Hamons sold gas and kindness to travelers for decades. Now preserved as a roadside stop on the old road.
places.section: Day 4 · Tulsa to Elk City, Oklahoma · 210 mi

places.name: Oklahoma Route 66 Museum
places.notes: A state-run museum with rooms that walk through the road decade by decade, from the Dust Bowl exodus to the neon motel era. Plan an hour or more.
places.section: Day 4 · Tulsa to Elk City, Oklahoma · 210 mi

places.name: National Route 66 & Transportation Museum
places.notes: A museum complex with a re-created old town, a farm and transportation museum, and a giant Route 66 sign for photos.
places.section: Day 4 · Tulsa to Elk City, Oklahoma · 210 mi

places.name: U-Drop Inn
places.notes: A 1936 Art Deco gas station and cafe, now the town visitor center. Come back after dark when the green and pink neon is on.
places.section: Day 5 · Elk City to Tucumcari, New Mexico · 260 mi

places.name: The Big Texan Steak Ranch
places.notes: The home of the 72-ounce steak challenge, with a motel and brewery on the same lot. Loud and kitschy, and that is the point.
places.section: Day 5 · Elk City to Tucumcari, New Mexico · 260 mi

places.name: Cadillac Ranch
places.notes: Ten Cadillacs buried nose-down in a field west of Amarillo by the Ant Farm art collective in 1974. Bring spray paint; everyone adds a layer.
places.section: Day 5 · Elk City to Tucumcari, New Mexico · 260 mi

places.name: Route 66 Midpoint
places.notes: A sign in tiny Adrian marks the halfway point: 1,139 miles to Chicago and 1,139 to Los Angeles.
places.section: Day 5 · Elk City to Tucumcari, New Mexico · 260 mi

places.name: Blue Swallow Motel
places.notes: A 1939 motor court with a garage beside each room and one of the best neon signs on the road. Book ahead in summer.
places.section: Day 5 · Elk City to Tucumcari, New Mexico · 260 mi

places.name: Motel Safari
places.notes: A 1959 motel restored with clean mid-century rooms and a camel on the sign. A good second choice if the Blue Swallow is full.
places.section: Day 5 · Elk City to Tucumcari, New Mexico · 260 mi

places.name: Tee Pee Curios
places.notes: A 1940s gift shop with a concrete tepee entrance and a neon sign that lights the street at night.
places.section: Day 5 · Elk City to Tucumcari, New Mexico · 260 mi

places.name: Del's Restaurant
places.notes: A family restaurant under a neon cow sign, serving New Mexican plates with red or green chile since 1956.
places.section: Day 5 · Elk City to Tucumcari, New Mexico · 260 mi

places.name: Blue Hole
places.address: 1085 Blue Hole Rd, Santa Rosa, NM 88435
places.notes: A clear, cold artesian spring about 80 feet deep, popular with scuba divers and for a bracing swim on a hot day.
places.section: Day 6 · Tucumcari to Gallup, New Mexico · 310 mi

places.name: Route 66 Auto Museum
places.notes: Rows of hot rods, classic cars and road signs in a big shed on the east side of town.
places.section: Day 6 · Tucumcari to Gallup, New Mexico · 310 mi

places.name: 66 Diner
places.notes: A 1950s-style diner on Central Avenue, Albuquerque's long stretch of 66, with burgers, green chile and thick shakes.
places.section: Day 6 · Tucumcari to Gallup, New Mexico · 310 mi

places.name: KiMo Theatre
places.notes: A 1927 theater in the Pueblo Deco style, with painted ceilings and steer-skull light fixtures. The city runs shows and occasional tours.
places.section: Day 6 · Tucumcari to Gallup, New Mexico · 310 mi

places.name: Richardson's Trading Company
places.notes: A trading post in business since 1913, with rooms full of Navajo rugs, Zuni jewelry and pawn.
places.section: Day 6 · Tucumcari to Gallup, New Mexico · 310 mi

places.name: El Rancho Hotel
places.notes: A 1937 hotel built for movie crews shooting westerns nearby. Rooms are named for the stars who stayed, and signed photos line the lobby balcony.
places.section: Day 6 · Tucumcari to Gallup, New Mexico · 310 mi

places.name: Petrified Forest National Park
places.address: 1 Park Rd, Petrified Forest National Park, AZ 86028
places.notes: The only national park that Route 66 crossed; an old Studebaker marks the alignment. Drive the park road from the Painted Desert to the log fields and exit to Holbrook.
places.section: Day 7 · Gallup to Flagstaff, Arizona · 190 mi

places.name: Wigwam Motel
places.notes: Fifteen concrete tepees from 1950, each with a vintage car parked out front. Book directly with the motel.
places.section: Day 7 · Gallup to Flagstaff, Arizona · 190 mi

places.name: Standin' on the Corner Park
places.notes: A street corner in Winslow made famous by the Eagles song, with a statue and a mural of a flatbed Ford.
places.section: Day 7 · Gallup to Flagstaff, Arizona · 190 mi

places.name: La Posada Hotel
places.notes: Mary Colter's 1930 railroad hotel, rescued and restored with gardens and art-filled halls. Trains still roll past the back door.
places.section: Day 7 · Gallup to Flagstaff, Arizona · 190 mi

places.name: The Turquoise Room
places.notes: The dining room at La Posada, cooking Southwestern food with local lamb and heirloom corn.
places.section: Day 7 · Gallup to Flagstaff, Arizona · 190 mi

places.name: Meteor Crater
places.notes: A crater almost a mile wide left by an impact about 50,000 years ago. A visitor center and observation decks sit on the rim, six miles south of the interstate.
places.section: Day 7 · Gallup to Flagstaff, Arizona · 190 mi

places.name: Lowell Observatory
places.address: 1400 W Mars Hill Rd, Flagstaff, AZ 86001
places.notes: The observatory on Mars Hill where Pluto was found in 1930. Come at night for telescope viewing under Flagstaff's dark skies.
places.section: Day 7 · Gallup to Flagstaff, Arizona · 190 mi

places.name: Hotel Monte Vista
places.address: 100 N San Francisco St, Flagstaff, AZ 86001
places.notes: A 1927 downtown hotel with a long list of movie-star guests and ghost stories. A block from the old 66 and the railroad.
places.section: Day 7 · Gallup to Flagstaff, Arizona · 190 mi

places.name: Grand Canyon Railway Depot
places.address: 233 N Grand Canyon Blvd, Williams, AZ 86046
places.notes: The 1908 depot where trains leave for the South Rim. Williams was the last Route 66 town bypassed by the interstate, and its main street still has the neon.
places.section: Day 8 · Flagstaff to Barstow, California · 390 mi

places.name: Delgadillo's Snow Cap
places.notes: A burger stand opened in 1953 by Juan Delgadillo, known for its pranks: fake mustard bottles and a menu of jokes. The family still runs it.
places.section: Day 8 · Flagstaff to Barstow, California · 390 mi

places.name: Angel & Vilma Delgadillo's Original Route 66 Gift Shop
places.notes: The former barbershop of Angel Delgadillo, who led the campaign to have the old road named a historic highway. Busy with souvenirs and stories.
places.section: Day 8 · Flagstaff to Barstow, California · 390 mi

places.name: Hackberry General Store
places.notes: A roadside store stacked with old gas pumps, signs and a red Corvette, on the long empty stretch between Peach Springs and Kingman.
places.section: Day 8 · Flagstaff to Barstow, California · 390 mi

places.name: Arizona Route 66 Museum
places.address: 120 W Andy Devine Ave, Kingman, AZ 86401
places.notes: A museum inside the 1907 Kingman powerhouse, covering the road from wagon trails to the motel era. The visitor center is in the same building.
places.section: Day 8 · Flagstaff to Barstow, California · 390 mi

places.name: Mr. D'z Route 66 Diner
places.address: 105 E Andy Devine Ave, Kingman, AZ 86401
places.notes: A turquoise and pink diner across from the powerhouse, serving burgers, root beer and breakfast.
places.section: Day 8 · Flagstaff to Barstow, California · 390 mi

places.name: Oatman Hotel
places.notes: A 1902 adobe in an old gold-mining town where wild burros wander the street. The bar walls are papered with signed dollar bills. Expect sharp switchbacks over Sitgreaves Pass to get here.
places.section: Day 8 · Flagstaff to Barstow, California · 390 mi

places.name: Roy's Motel and Café
places.notes: A 1959 boomerang sign in the Mojave, at a stop with a small store and gas. Parts of National Trails Highway close for repairs; check San Bernardino County road status.
places.section: Day 8 · Flagstaff to Barstow, California · 390 mi

places.name: Elmer's Bottle Tree Ranch
places.address: 24266 National Trails Hwy, Oro Grande, CA 92368
places.notes: A field of welded metal trees hung with colored glass bottles, built by Elmer Long. Free to wander; stay on the paths.
places.section: Day 9 · Barstow to Santa Monica · 140 mi

places.name: California Route 66 Museum
places.notes: A small volunteer-run museum on old 66 in Victorville with a VW hippie van, signs and road memorabilia.
places.section: Day 9 · Barstow to Santa Monica · 140 mi

places.name: Wigwam Motel
places.address: 2728 W Foothill Blvd, San Bernardino, CA 92410
places.notes: The 1949 California sibling of the Holbrook motel: concrete tepees around a pool on Foothill Boulevard, the old 66.
places.section: Day 9 · Barstow to Santa Monica · 140 mi

places.name: Fair Oaks Pharmacy
places.notes: A 1915 drugstore with a restored soda fountain on the old route through South Pasadena. Phosphates, malts and egg creams at the counter.
places.section: Day 9 · Barstow to Santa Monica · 140 mi

places.name: Barney's Beanery
places.address: 8447 Santa Monica Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069
places.notes: A roadhouse on Santa Monica Boulevard, the last leg of Route 66, at this spot since 1927. Chili, pool tables and license plates on the ceiling.
places.section: Day 9 · Barstow to Santa Monica · 140 mi

places.name: Santa Monica Pier
places.address: 200 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401
places.notes: The end of the road. The Route 66 End of the Trail sign stands on the pier, past the carousel; walk out for the ocean and the Ferris wheel.
places.section: Day 9 · Barstow to Santa Monica · 140 mi
